Hi Andrew,

you need to rebase your change with master branch i think...

and also convert dissector to built in (and not dissector plugin)

Yes, I would plan to do that before submitting 'officially'. The main reason for putting it on here at the moment is to get comments on the structure of the code, to see if I'm doing anything 'wrong'.

Once the plugin is complete, I will rebase against master before submitting officially.

Also, I would convert to a builtin rather than a plugin before submitting. It's helpful having it as a plugin as I can just copy the DLL across after compiling to test.

At this point it's a little hard to see the forest from the trees because the diff shows all of the other commits that aren't your dissector (plugin or built in).  You may also find APIs may have changed slightly in 3400+ commits so that may force some updates to your existing dissector.
Fixed that for you.

The merge information gives the impression this commit would be added to the 4.4 release, which is not correct.  All new functionality should be added to the master branch (and should be rebased accordingly)

This is deliberate for now. I'm building against 4.4 as I seem to recall having some issues building 'master'. 

If and when I want to merge this 'proper', I would rebase against master.

I've a few comments already (call me grumpy).  
- The way this code is structured does almost requires it to be confined to a plugin (which can be okay)
- Redefining stdint types to some derivatives does not make portable/readable code
- Using structures to overlay packet layout (even with pragma packed, which is non-portable by the way) is just not cutting it. 
- Dissectors should be written in C11, only the ui/qt part of the codebase is setup for C++.

This is exactly why I wanted to get the code looked at before I got too far, to 'catch' these sorts of things early.

1. What about the structure requires it to be a plugin? Could I restructure it to avoid this?
2. Point taken about the stdint types, will rethink that
3. I saw the warning about using structures. I guess the other way is just to 'know' the offsets of everything in the packets? Will (I think) make the code a little less readable, but I'll have a think about that.
4. Is it really a requirement not to use C++ in the dissectors? I don't use many C++ features presently, so it's probably not a big deal.

Thanks for your input, appreciate it.

With the current dissector architecture, there really isn't a need for C++ and most of what you have here is "sugar syntax" and unnecessary encapsulation.  I still think of dissector code as a "script" that just happens to be written in C.  You don't really need header files because the data structures are unique to your dissector(s) and don't need to be shared.  And if you're not saving data for future/further dissection, the "script" doesn't really need data structures, the code is more like "Display field X of two bytes, adjust offset 2 bytes, display field Y of 4 bytes, etc...".  And from the consecutive calls to display fields, you can implicitly see what the "data structure" is for the data in a packet.
And as you can see, Wireshark already has hundreds of dissectors and even if each dissector only had 1 C file, that's hundreds of files to maintain, so we discourage additional source files that are only "helper functions" to a single dissector.  All "EA F1 sports dissection" should be able to fit in a single C file, even if it is 12000 lines, because it will still have a flow of
1. Declaring hf fields, value_strings, etc
2. Dissection helper functions and subdissection functions
3. Main dissector function
4. Descriptions of individual fields and protocol registration/hooks

and the maintainers of the Wireshark code base can quickly read through that (there are also "helper tools/scripts" that can catch developer bugs if dissectors are written in that format.)

I've made a commit that removes the reliance on C structures for the Header and LobbyInfo parsing (see `dissect_eaf1` and `dissect_eaf1_2025_lobbyinfo`).

Do these look like a more 'correct' way to do it? If so, I'll update the remainder of the packet types, which will remove the reliance on the structures.

I was planning to split the different game formats (F1 23, F1 24 etc.) into different files, but if generally the 'done thing' is to have them all in one file, then I can certainly do that. The 'helper' functions can then just be at the top of that single file.

That'll probably remove the need for C++ too. About all I was using was namespaces to isolate the structure definitions for the different game versions, and the odd 'auto' here and there. I'll look at converting it to a 'c' file if that's more the 'done' thing.

Also because packet-eaf1.cc is too large to leave comments on (which I can't say I've seen before), you'll want to use a string_string structure (similar to value_string, but for strings) for dissect_eaf1_2025_event() because it will reduce your if/else blocks.
There are many different "whitespace formatting of hf_ fields" (and there are dissectors with this same formatting), but I think a line per field may be a bit much given the number of fields in the dissector.

I didn't like the structure of the event string handling code. I'll have a look for an example of somewhere that uses `string_string` to see how it will help.

I'm not sure what your comment about 'many different whitespace formatting of hf_ fields' means exactly?

I can't see how using `string_string` would necessarily help with in `dissect_eaf1_2025_event()`? It looks like I could use a string based dissector table to split the handling of the different events into different functions though. That might make things more obvious.

This could perhaps then be further optimised by handling all of the events with no parameters in a single function, and lookup the 'event type' (for `COL_INFO`) using a `string_string`?

It was more about not having to make the proto_item_set_text call so many times (there were several if/else that would otherwise be blank and that was the simplification I was after.  String based dissector table would also work (and add some more flexibility), and I would consider looking at proto_register_protocol_in_name_only for it.

The 'many different whitespace formatting of hf\_ fields' comment meant that there isn't (unfortunately?) a "standard" for the whitespace formatting of hf\_ fields, so you can find many different formats between the hundreds of dissectors. I just think only using 2 or 3 lines per field makes it easier to see more fields at once on your screen.

I've restructured the event handling function to use a string_string array to find the column text, and also used a dissector table to break the handling into individual functions.

How does that look now?

You need to fix 
`packet-eaf1.cc                     : {NULL, NULL} is required as the last string_string array entry: string_string event_desc_lookup[]`

Yeah, saw that in the pipeline failure. I wish I could run the CLang build and all its checks locally!

Now fixed, thanks.

+include(WiresharkPlugin)
+
+# Plugin name and version info (major minor micro extra)
+set_module_info(eaf1 0 0 1 0)
+
+set(DISSECTOR_SRC
+	packet-eaf1.cc
+)
+
+set(PLUGIN_FILES
+	plugin.c
+	${DISSECTOR_SRC}
+)
+
+set_source_files_properties(
+	${PLUGIN_FILES}
+	PROPERTIES
+	COMPILE_FLAGS "${WERROR_COMMON_FLAGS}"
+)
+
+register_plugin_files(plugin.c
+	plugin
+	${DISSECTOR_SRC}
+)
+
+add_wireshark_plugin_library(eaf1 epan)
+
+target_link_libraries(eaf1 epan)
+target_include_directories(eaf1 PUBLIC f1-telemetry-protocol)
+
+install_plugin(eaf1 epan)
+
+file(GLOB DISSECTOR_HEADERS RELATIVE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}" "*.h")
+CHECKAPI(
+	NAME
+	  eaf1
+	SWITCHES
+	  --group dissectors-prohibited
+	  --group dissectors-restricted
+	SOURCES
+	  ${DISSECTOR_SRC}
+	  ${DISSECTOR_HEADERS}
+)
